text:
incident-bot: SEV-1 alert: high queue depth and 500 spikes for /v1/generate (us-west-2) — autoscaler failing to add capacity :rotating_light:
elena: I got paged, joining. seeing lots of 503/504 from inference cluster.
raj: confirmed. queue length ~3.5k requests, GPU pool at 100% and autoscaler at scale cap 20. no new replicas launching.
sam: past 10m throughput down ~40% vs baseline. latency climbing, throttling kicking in.
elena: any recent deploys?
deploy-bot: rollout: batching-config-service v2.3.1 -> v2.4.0 deployed by ci/cd at 2026-03-15T02:10:12Z.
raj: that batching-config change included continuous-batching param tweaks and prefix-cache TTL drop to 4s. suspect regression.
sam: logs show rapid prefix cache misses, KV cache eviction churn. example from router: "kv_cache_miss_ratio=0.78, batch_size=1-3, cpu_wait=high"
elena: can someone post the config diff?
raj: paste: ```
- continuous_batching.enabled: true
- continuous_batching.batch_window_ms: 8
- prefix_cache.ttl_ms: 30000
+ continuous_batching.enabled: true
+ continuous_batching.batch_window_ms: 2
+ prefix_cache.ttl_ms: 4000
```
sam: batch_window shrink combined with tiny prefix TTL means per-request overhead skyrockets. continuous batching not effective for our long-tail seq lengths.
jen: agreed. mitigation plan: 1) raise autoscaler cap / temporarily increase pool size; 2) rollback batching-config or patch TTL + batch_window; 3) warm prefix cache / prime hot keys; 4) notifications to impacted customers.
elena: I'm going to lift the autoscale cap to avoid immediate queueing. doing: `redwoodctl autoscaler update --region us-west-2 --max-instances 40`
deploy-bot: autoscaler update accepted, new max-instances=40 in progress.
raj: while that scales, I can patch batching-config to restore previous TTL and batch_window. prepping a quick patch.
sam: also recommend temporarily disable continuous batching on this service while we validate. less efficient but more predictable right now.
elena: patch applied: `kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: batching-config
data:
  continuous_batching.enabled: "false"
  prefix_cache.ttl_ms: "30000"
EOF`
deploy-bot: configmap updated, rolling config to inference pods.
raj: observing immediate change: prefix cache hit rate improving, batch sizes recovering. queue dropping from 3500 -> 1200 in 3m.
sam: error rate down but still elevated for a subset of heavy customers: we'll need to keep scaling until warm cache stabilizes.
support-lead: customer impact: support telemetry shows ~8 enterprise customers with elevated error rates; roughly 1100 affected requests/minute at peak. Opening support incident and templating outbound.
elena: good. tagging support and SRE for postmortem. @support-lead can you start a bridge with affected accounts?
support-lead: on it. draft message: "We experienced degraded generation performance in us-west-2; mitigation in progress; updates every 15m."
raj: one more thing — autoscaler didn't trigger earlier because desired replicas were blocked by per-cluster scale-limit setting in cluster-config. I'm filing a follow-up to remove brittle hard cap.
sam: for now we've scaled to 34 instances manually and queue is down to ~400, error rates trending back to baseline.
jen: handoff to night oncall @raj — summary: deploy v2.4.0 changed continuous batching/window and prefix TTL; caused cache miss storm + smaller batches -> throughput down -> queue growth -> autoscaler hit hard cap. Mitigations done: increased autoscale cap, disabled continuous batching, restored prefix TTL, warmed cache, support notified. Followups: permanent config policy, e2e perf test before batching rollouts, remove hard cluster caps, post-incident RCA.
raj: taking over oncall. I'll monitor for 2h and coordinate RCA. anyone else?
elena: will stay reachable for 30m.
sam: adding perf graphs to the incident doc and capturing before/after numbers.
support-lead: outbound sent to affected customers, included ETA and mitigation steps.
raj: next immediate task: validate rollback sequence for v2.4.0 and schedule a controlled rollout with canary throttles. created ticket INF-4821.
jen: thanks all — closing paging loop. add emoji reaction :white_check_mark: when you've read the handoff.
elena: :white_check_mark:
raj: :white_check_mark:
sam: :white_check_mark:
support-lead: :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident cleared: queue below threshold and error rate within SLO. Please file postmortem within 72h.
